front.head: Introduction to this file
front.p:
This document contains the translation table for converting various boilerplate or forme work phrases into various languages. It is a TEI file that may contain all sorts of stuff (including this paragraph) that is not actually part of the translation mechanism. The only part the XSLT looks at is /TEI/text/body/list[ @type eq 'i18n']. That list should contain a sequence of item elements, each of which is required to have:
a unique identifier on an xml:id attribute
an optional desc element for describing what the particular gloss is for
one or more gloss elements, each of which should have an xml:lang attribute; at least one of which has a value that is en or starts with en-this is not strictly necessary per XML, as this whole file is in English. Thus if you left the xml:lang off of one gloss, that one would be the English one. But having it explicit makes the data lot easier to proofread, and protects against future corruption if and when the data is copied to a non-English environment)..
There should never be two or more gloss siblings that have the same xml:lang. Although not necessary for processing, it is convenient for human readers if the desc element comes before all the gloss elements, and the en gloss is the first.

Note that these requirements are required by our processor. We do not currently have a schema that enforces these conditions. But it would not be particularly difficult to come up with one if the editors would so prefer.
Note also that we admit that these entries are not really glosses, so gloss is mild tag abuse. But TEI does not have a useThisText, and reg is similarly slightly off target.
